places.rationale: A rich, capable state with a strong AI sector, but a productivity stall since 2008, high debt, 48% energy imports and exposure as a nuclear power and to an AMOC slowdown keep the downside meaningful.
Nuclear power and strong redistribution help both resilience and the 9-in-10 abundance bar, while rising debt and weak political stability raise stagnation risk.

Extreme inequality makes the 9-in-10 abundance bar very hard, and fifteen years of flat income per head, severe water stress, violent crime and a heavy interest burden keep stagnation and collapse risks high.
A quarter-century of flat income per head, debt near 140% of GDP, severe aging, 79% energy imports and Mediterranean heat and drought make stagnation unusually likely without superintelligence.

A low starting point and steady catch-up growth make 'better' the default, but abundance needs roughly 36 times today's consumption, and high climate vulnerability, food insecurity and a 24% interest burden keep collapse risk around one in ten.
Ample water and decent health coverage support steady gains, while armed violence, weak stability, high inequality and dependence on oil and coal exports that will fade limit the upside.

Chips and robotics put Korea in a strong position if superintelligence arrives, but the world's lowest fertility, 83% energy imports and a nuclear-armed North Korea weigh heavily, especially without it.
A peaceful, open society with large solar potential and immigration offsetting low fertility, but water stress heading toward 4.5 and a southern climate hotspot are the main drags.
Food, shale and lithium wealth and a temperate climate give real resilience, but decades of macroeconomic crises and flat income per head make long stagnation unusually plausible.
Abundant energy, water, land and minerals, low climate vulnerability and strong institutions place it among the safest, though weak productivity and dependence on the US are the main risks.

Today's wartime baseline is low, so reconstruction and EU integration make 'better' likely, but renewed Russian aggression, demographic collapse and weak governance keep collapse risk the highest in Europe.

Low debt, huge solar potential and big AI investment help, but fading oil rents, near-maximum water stress, extreme Gulf heat, regional war risk and a 40% migrant workforce that counts toward the 9-in-10 bar widen the downside.
Thirty years of strong catch-up growth, low debt and stability favour continued gains, while sharp aging and being on NATO's front line with Russia raise the tail risk.
A rich energy, food and mineral exporter in the Southern Hemisphere, relatively shielded from nuclear war and famine, though heat, fire and drought exposure is high for a rich country.

Very effective governance, low debt and a key role in chipmaking support the upside, while sea-level rise, with a quarter of the land below sea level, and 88% energy imports are the specific tail risks.
High equality, low debt, clean domestic energy and low water stress favour both resilience and broad abundance, with Baltic security and gang violence the visible weak points.

The highest living standard here, a huge sovereign fund, hydropower and high equality make the abundance bar closest, while a high starting point and the end of oil make stagnation its main risk without superintelligence.
